text:
Megan (Support): FYI customer AcmePay reporting sudden 429s and long tail latency right after last night's runtime cutover. They say it looks like a hard throughput cutoff.
Kai - Infra: on it, can you paste a repro curl + response headers?
Megan (Support): here's the snippet they sent: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-1","input":"hi"}'
```
Megan (Support): Response snippet: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-Redwood-ReservedPool-Headroom: 0
{"error":{"message":"throughput capped: reserved pool exhausted","code":429}}
```
Sam R: that X header showing ReservedPool-Headroom: 0 is the red flag. Looks like burst headroom isn't available for their dedicated pool.
Elena P: was the canary traffic routed to the new capacity profile? I thought we left a small reserve for cutovers.
Kai - Infra: config check: account AcmePay has reserved_pool_quota=600rps, burst_window=60s, smoothing=fast. After cutover they switched to node-pool v2 which enforces stricter burst gating. infra-bot: matched runtime change at 2026-03-15T02:12:40Z -> enforced token-bucket with max_burst_tokens=600.
Megan (Support): customer timeline: spikes started at 02:18, sustained for ~7m, then got a bunch of 429s. They were running a canary with small fanout (10 qps each) but steady.
Raj T: two hypotheses: 1) token-bucket underflow because refill rate misaligned with sustain rate during node handoff, 2) routing mis-classified their requests into shared headroom quota.
Kai - Infra: pulled runtime logs for their pool: 
```
[02:18:05] pool=dedicated-acmepay node=nodex-12 event=gate_throttle reason=reserved_pool_exhausted tokens=0 refill=10/s
[02:18:12] event=request_reject status=429 route=/v1/generate id=req-9a7cb
[02:20:30] event=pool_recovery tokens=45 headroom=0
```
Elena P: also saw controller audit: during cutover we briefly drained one leaf and rebalanced tokens; controller mistakenly applied strict smoothing to that pool for 5m. That matches the 7m window.
Megan (Support): customer asking if this is a billing/account throttle or platform SLO enforcement. Need a clear explainer and immediate mitigation.
Sam R: short answer: platform gating (reserved pool) not billing. We throttle to protect SLAs. But we can grant a temporary headroom bump for emergency.
Kai - Infra: mitigation options: 
- immediate: add emergency_headroom +200 tokens to dedicated-acmepay (manual)
- short-term: relax smoothing from "fast" to "normal" for 15m during cutover windows
- medium: increase reserved_pool_quota to 900rps and/or increase max_burst_tokens
ops-bot: emergency headroom change requires approval tag and audit log.
Megan (Support): I'll ask AcmePay if they can pause canary for 10m while we apply patch. If they want immediate unblocked traffic we'll do emergency_headroom.
Raj T: also add a postmortem action: ensure cutover playbook toggles smoothing back to previous value. Add a safety check to detect 0 headroom within 2m of a node drain.
Kai - Infra: reproduction steps for infra to validate: 
1) simulate node drain -> reassign tokens
2) run sustained 12qps fanout for 10m
3) check token-bucket refill behavior and X-Redwood-ReservedPool-Headroom header
We should automate that in chaos tests.
Megan (Support): customer agreed to pause canary; asking for timeline and whether they'll see billing credits.
Sam R: no billing credits needed; they were throttled by capacity gating. Offer them a 1-hour emergency capacity waiver (internal contract) and document incident.
Elena P: I'm going to flip the smoothing flag to normal for their pool now and add +250 headroom. I'll annotate in audit.
infra-bot: applied change: pool=dedicated-acmepay smoothing=normal headroom_delta=+250 applied_by=ElenaP at 1769457010
Megan (Support): sending update to customer: we applied temporary headroom +250 and relaxed smoothing. Please test and report any 429s.
AcmePay (via support DM): quick test shows fewer 429s but some latency spikes remain.
Kai - Infra: remaining latency likely due to KV cache warmup after node replacement. That should settle in ~10-15m.
Raj T: follow ups: 1) run post-cutover audit to ensure pool headroom never hits zero, 2) add canary checklist step to reserve +X tokens during handoffs, 3) update runbook for emergency_headroom procedure.
Megan (Support): creating support ticket #SUP-12458 with summary and actions. I'll close thread after customer confirms stable for 30m. :thumbsup:
Sam R: nice work team.
Elena P: adding postmortem note to ops board.
Megan (Support): closing note: If we change default smoothing in runtime, notify PM and CS teams first to avoid surprises.
